extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from local XML/PDF/OA figure captions and text.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: MR-22 has direct source-supported evidence for damaging E. coli membrane integrity and increasing permeability under the paper conditions.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: MR-22 against E. coli ATCC 25922 and E19
mechanism_claims.limitations: Directly supports membrane integrity/permeability disruption; it does not identify a specific molecular receptor target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: PI-positive cell percentages increased with 1x, 2x, and 4x MIC MR-22 in both ATCC 25922 and E19, supporting dose-responsive permeability effects.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: MR-22 against E. coli ATCC 25922 and E19
mechanism_claims.limitations: Percentages are membrane-permeability readouts, not standalone MIC endpoints.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper reports increased ROS and decreased intracellular ATP after MR-22 treatment, with NAC reducing ROS-related antibacterial activity.
mechanism_claims.limitations: ROS/ATP changes are source-supported downstream cellular effects; they are not normalized to a direct target identity.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: MR-22 improved survival and lowered peritoneal bacterial burden in the E. coli E19 mouse peritonitis model at 10 mg/kg.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: MR-22 in C57BL/6J mouse peritonitis model
mechanism_claims.limitations: In vivo efficacy is preserved as therapeutic context, not a direct molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The article schematic frames membrane disruption, ROS accumulation, and ATP perturbation as a plausible cascade leading to E. coli death.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The cascade language is kept as a model/caution and is not expanded beyond the assays in Figures 3-6.
